data.name: Magid
data.gender_notes: Magid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'mawgid', meaning 'guide' or 'leader'. In Islamic tradition, Magid is a name given to those who lead others to the right path. The name Magid carries the meaning “Guide, Leader” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Magid usually hope their child will grow to embody guide, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name given to those who guide others to the right path in life.
data.etymology: Magid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guide, Leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Magid total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: ماجد
in_arabic.meaning: الله تعالیٰ کی تعریف کرنے والا، بلند مرتبہ والا
in_arabic.long_meaning: ماجد اسم ہے جو اللہ تعالیٰ کی تعریف کرنے والے اور بلند مرتبہ والے کے معنی میں ہے۔ اس کا عربی جڑ 'م-ج-د' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'تعریف کرنا' یا 'عظمت'. قرآن میں اس جڑ کا ذکر تعریف اور عظمت کے سیاق میں آیا ہے۔ ماجد نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ اللہ کی عظمت اور تعریف کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔

in_urdu.name: مجید
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ تعالیٰ کی تعریف کرنے والا، بہت باعزت
in_urdu.long_meaning: مجید ایک اسلامی نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے اللہ تعالیٰ کی تعریف کرنے والا یا بہت باعزت۔ یہ نام عربی جڑ 'م-ج-د' سے بنا ہے جس کا تعلق تعریف اور عظمت سے ہے۔ اسلامی دنیا میں اس نام کا استعمال شائع ہے کیونکہ یہ اللہ کی عظمت اور شان کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ تاریخی طور پر، یہ نام مختلف اسلامی سلاطین اور علما کے لیے استعمال ہوا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: माजिद
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की स्तुति करने वाला, उच्च पद वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: माजिद एक महत्वपूर्ण इस्लामी नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से आया है। इसका अर्थ है भगवान की स्तुति करने वाला या उच्च पद वाला। यह नाम अरबी मूल 'म-ज-द' से बना है जो स्तुति और महिमा से जुड़ा है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का उपयोग आम है क्योंकि यह भगवान की महिमा और स्तुति को दर्शाता है। ऐतिहासिक रूप से, यह नाम इस्लामी शासकों और विद्वानों के लिए प्रयोग किया गया है।

in_pashto.name: ماجد
in_pashto.meaning: د الله تعالی ستایښی کوونکی، لوړ پوړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ماجد د اسلامي نومونو څخه يو دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دغه نوم د 'م-ج-د' په عربي اصل کې د ستايښی او لوړتیا معنی لري. په پښتنو او افغانانو کې د دغه نوم کارول د عربي او اسلامي کلتور سره تړاو لري. دا نوم د الهي لوړتیا او ستايښی څرګندوي.

in_english.name: Magid
in_english.meaning: One who praises God, glorious, exalted
in_english.long_meaning: Magid is an Arabic-originated name meaning 'one who praises God' or 'glorious'. It stems from the root 'm-j-d', which implies 'to praise' or 'glory'. This name holds significance in Islamic tradition as it reflects divine praise and glory. Historically, it has been used by various Islamic scholars and rulers. The name signifies a person of high moral character and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Magid holds significant cultural importance in the Islamic world as it reflects the importance of being a guide or leader for others in one's community. This name is often given to those who are seen as role models, mentors, or teachers, emphasizing their responsibility to guide and lead others towards positive actions and behaviors.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Magid is deeply rooted in Islamic beliefs of guiding others to the right path, which aligns with one of the fundamental teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, "Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good and driving away that which is evil, bounteous towards the believers in their affection, steadfast upon Deen." (3:104) By being given the name Magid, one is entrusted with the responsibility of upholding these values and living up to the example set by the Prophet.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Book 11, Chapter 9, Hadith 1265. Mawlana Muhammad al-Maghribi (d. 612 AH/1216 CE) was a preacher, poet, and Sufi teacher from Morocco. He was a student of Ibn al-Arabi and was known for his extraordinary ecstatic experiences and profound spiritual insight. He is also known as Ibn al-Maghrib (Son of the Maghreb), and was a popular preacher in Damascus and in Egypt.
historical_references.context: Moroccan Sufi teacher, student of Ibn al-Arabi

historical_references.reference: Al-Qalqashandi, Subh al-A'sha, Volume 8, page 397. Al-Maghdi (d. 520 AH/1126 CE) was a Berber ruler of the Almoravid dynasty in the western region of the Islamic world, which includes present-day Morocco and Andalusia. He came to power in 511 AH/1117 CE and ruled until his death in 520 AH/1126 CE. He is also known as Al-Mansur Billah (The Victorious by God) and is remembered for his military conquests and his patronage of scholarship and culture.
historical_references.context: Berber ruler of the Almoravid dynasty
